Frequently asked questions

Recognition & validity

Are online degrees valid in India?

Yes — if the university is entitled or recognised by the UGC Distance Education Bureau (UGC-DEB) for that programme and session. UGC has declared such degrees equivalent to conventional degrees. All universities on Degree Plus are on the UGC-DEB 2026-27 online list.

How can I check that a university is really UGC approved?

Open deb.ugc.ac.in and look at the list “HEIs Entitled for Online Programmes AY 2026-27”. Search the university and the exact programme. Never rely on a logo alone — check the list before you pay any fee.

What is the difference between Online, Distance (ODL) and Regular?

Regular means attending a campus. ODL (distance) uses study material and contact classes. Online uses a Learning Management System with live and recorded classes and online exams. A university needs separate UGC-DEB permission for each mode.

Will employers and government jobs accept an online degree?

Because UGC treats the degree as equivalent, most private employers and many public recruiters accept it. Each recruiting body sets its own eligibility rules, so check the advertisement for the post you want.

Abroad & visas

Can I use an online degree to study abroad?

Many students do. A degree from a UGC-recognised university is widely accepted when applying for a Master’s abroad, but each foreign university decides whether it accepts the online mode. Always confirm with the target university before you enrol.

Is the degree usable for a work visa or immigration?

Skilled-worker visas usually need your degree to be assessed (for example by WES in Canada). A UGC-recognised degree can be assessed, but outcomes depend on the country, the assessor and the visa category — some treat online and regular degrees differently. We help you check the rules for your target country before you pick a course.

Do I need my degree attested or apostilled?

For most countries, yes. The university issues the degree and transcripts; attestation and apostille are done through the relevant government departments. Ask your university about its process during admission.

Fees & admission

How much does an online degree cost?

It varies by programme and university — for example, LPU online MBA is listed at ₹40,400 per semester and online MCA at ₹32,400 per semester. Fees change each session, so we show the latest figure we could verify and our counsellor confirms the exact amount with you.

Is EMI or a scholarship available?

Most universities offer semester-wise payment and EMI, and some give discounts or scholarships (for example for sports or academic achievements). Terms differ — ask us for the current offer.

Which documents are needed for admission?

Usually: 10th and 12th marksheets, graduation marksheets (for PG), Aadhaar, passport photo and a signature. The university will verify them through the UGC-DEB ID process.

Do I pay Degree Plus anything?

No. Comparing universities and speaking to a counsellor on Degree Plus is free for students. Course fees are paid directly to the university — never to an individual.

Studying online

How are exams conducted?

Online programmes use online or proctored exams plus internal assessments. Exact format (home-based or exam centre) differs by university, so check this before you enrol.

How many hours a week do I need to study?

Roughly 8–10 hours a week is typical (LPU recommends this for its MBA). You can fit it around a job.

I live in a village — can I still study online?

Yes. A smartphone or laptop and a stable 4G / broadband connection is enough. Recorded lectures help if the network drops.
